clue.text: Tests aid drunk to establish aversion

indicators.note: someone drunk is all over the place, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sets drinking tests in order to prove a dislike of alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges TESTSAID; 'to establish' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of dislike or repugnance, which is what an aversion is.

clue.text: A church hanging, or so lads made out

indicators.note: made out suggests the letters are worked into a different shape

explanation.surface: Some boys claim a church drape is really something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made out' rearranges SOLADS; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossal is an ornamental cloth hung behind an altar in a church.

parts.note: to sting someone into action is to provoke them
nothing, zero, looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A drink, but no provocation, please.
explanation.walkthrough: STINGO is an old name for strong ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is a strong old English beer, a kind of alcoholic beverage.

definitions.meaning: a point of view or standpoint
to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: An opinion formed about some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a perspective on something, and to angle is to fish with hook and line.

indicators.note: about tells us one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a tone is a musical sound
a nag is a horse, especially an old one

explanation.surface: Noise surrounding the size of a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'Sound' looks like a verb but supplies a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage measures a ship's carrying capacity in tons.

indicators.note: about indicates the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: weary means tired
a commercial is an advertisement, an AD

explanation.surface: Someone tired of a television advertisement hurls insults.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech of criticism, verbal abuse.

clue.text: Being unsettled in it, aren't getting all sorted out

indicators.note: sorted out suggests the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Being unsettled about something, it's not getting organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all sorted out' rearranges INITARENT; 'Being' and 'getting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant means travelling from place to place, without a settled home.

clue.text: Gun not recently used — put in a silencer

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: a mute is a device that silences or softens an instrument
to set something is to put it down

explanation.surface: An old gun gets a silencer fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not recently used' belongs to the definition: the gun is obsolete. 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusette was a light field cannon of the 18th century, long since out of service.

parts.note: people voting in secret put a cross on a ballot paper, making their mark in private

explanation.surface: People who will succeed discreetly.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters mark their ballot paper with a cross in the privacy of a polling booth.

clue.text: Head of state going by air, going to and fro

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: winging is flying

explanation.surface: A head of state flies about on official trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Something swinging moves back and forth like a pendulum.

definitions.meaning: a written record or memo, as of a meeting

explanation.surface: A message saying there's hardly any time left.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is a written memo, and also sixty seconds, a short spell.

clue.text: The bank's right, raising the charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A bank is right to increase its charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' suits a down clue, where the word reads upwards. The 'bank' is undersea, not financial.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or sand near the surface of the sea, a kind of bank.

definitions.meaning: to gather together into a whole
crushed stone or gravel used in making concrete

explanation.surface: Gather gravel for builders.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggregate is to gather into a mass, and aggregate is crushed stone used by builders in concrete.

clue.text: Leave of absence from lunch say

parts.note: ex is a Latin preposition meaning out of or from
to lunch is an example of eating

explanation.surface: Time off from work for a lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: An EXEAT is the permission British boarding schools give a pupil to go away, often for a weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeat is Latin for 'let him go out': formal permission to be absent from school or college.

indicators.note: in printing, pie is type that has been jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A meat pie with no flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' is printers' jargon for jumbled type, so it rearranges MEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame can mean dull and uninspiring, as flat writing or a flat performance is.

clue.text: Finding a party about over, left

indicators.note: about indicates the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a band is a group or party of people
something done is over, finished

explanation.surface: Discovering that a celebration is over and everyone has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'Finding' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abandoned has been deserted, left behind by its owners.

explanation.surface: A smoother operator lays on the praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatter is the comparative of level, and to flatter is to praise insincerely.

clue.text: Not the accommodation for down-to earth travellers!

definitions.text: Not the accommodation for down-to earth travellers!

parts.words: Not the accommodation for down-to earth travellers!
parts.note: travellers who stay on the ground, not those who fly, have no use for this room up above

explanation.surface: Lodging unsuitable for practical, unpretentious tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspace is the region of sky above a country through which aircraft fly, of no use to ground travellers.

clue.text: Words of praise by no means rare

definitions.meaning: a congratulation spoken to someone who succeeds
of meat, cooked thoroughly rather than underdone

explanation.surface: Praising something that is quite common.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase congratulates someone, and describes steak cooked right through rather than bloody.

parts.note: ire is anger
a sovereign is a gold pound coin, and L stands for pound

explanation.surface: A monarch and a nation stirring up fury.
explanation.walkthrough: L (from Latin libra) is the pound sign's letter, and a sovereign is a British gold coin worth one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a nation in north-west Europe.

definitions.meaning: to ... hopes is to crush or frustrate them

explanation.surface: Rapid progress toward losing.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to rush quickly, and to dash someone's hopes is to defeat them.

parts.note: a bit is a little amount
east is one of the four compass quarters, E

explanation.surface: Being injured in battle when the enemy gives scant mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: The four compass points are often called quarters, so E (east) is a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bite is an injury made by teeth, a kind of wound.

clue.text: Group of soldiers demolishing a bridge

indicators.note: demolishing breaks something up, so these letters are knocked down and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A military unit blowing up a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is an army unit of several battalions.

clue.text: Sack the painter seen in a girl's embrace

indicators.note: a girl's embrace holds something inside her name

parts.note: Maud is a girl's name
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's standard painter

explanation.surface: An artist is seen being hugged by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embrace' puts RA inside MAUD; 'seen in' is a link. RA stands for a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, which is what marauders do.

parts.note: a landlord is one who lets property, and correspondence is written messages

explanation.surface: Mail sent by a property owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter is a written message, and a letter is also one who lets out property.

parts.note: so means provided that, as in 'so long as'
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A cover was supplied for a horse's stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid means firm and steady, so stable.

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients, so these letters ferment into a new order

explanation.surface: Making beer, it must make people think.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate is to rouse the mind, to make people think.

parts.note: U stands for upper class, socially superior
a sage is a wise person or philosopher

explanation.surface: A top thinker is given a job.
explanation.walkthrough: U (upper class) is a British label for socially superior speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is used, its employment.

parts.note: a mount is a hill, a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: An increase in loudness.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a quantity, which is what volume measures.

clue.text: Such a fall can affect the eyesight

definitions.text: Such a fall can affect the eyesight

parts.words: Such a fall can affect the eyesight
parts.note: a waterfall, and also a clouding of the eye's lens that impairs vision

explanation.surface: A tumble that could damage one's vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a large waterfall and also an opacity of the eye's lens.

clue.text: Reforms — some of them end serious injustices

indicators.note: some of says only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Changes, some of which end grave unfairness.
explanation.definitionFit: Emends means corrects or improves, as reforms do.

clue.text: The guard put off accepting a tip

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to defer is to put off or postpone
an end is a tip or extremity

explanation.surface: The sentry postponed taking a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' is the container signal; 'The guard' is a person, not a device.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender is one who guards or protects.
